tasks.short: Pay duties and taxes on shipments

steps.what: Open duty notices for the shipments
Check taxes against the duty notice
Arrange payment of duties on the shipments

tasks.design: The duty notice for a shipment id is opened from {ERP} and {GOV_PORTAL}. The broker checks the taxes and arranges payment in {BANK}. A notice that does not match the shipment is not paid.
tasks.previous_blocker: The amount lived in a notice and a mail trail, so the payment waited on someone to re-key it.
tasks.enabler_now: The notice is tied to the shipment id, so the broker sees the figure without re-keying it.
tasks.still_hard: The authority's account details and a short payment still need the broker.
tasks.human_edge: The broker decides that this notice is the one to pay.
tasks.altitude: The broker sees every duty notice before any money moves.

evidence.claim: Paying a published duty is a checked figure plus a person who releases the money. The source pack says duty and tax figures are configured from a public tariff and contracted rates, and that a classification is taken from a stored binding decision only when one matches, with the broker signing the code.

The source pack says a solely automated decision with a significant effect on a person needs a human review. A duty figure here is a stored rate times a stored value, and the broker signs before a filing, a payment, or a quote leaves. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a duty notice arrives for a shipment and ends when the broker has arranged that payment.
The notice has shipment id, tax lines, and amount, produced by the customs authority. A notice that is only a scan is read by the broker.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the broker's effort.
A missing rate, code, or document is not invented. The broker does that part.
The incremental hour updates the record when its source row changes.
unknowns: Whether the authority accepts the payment reference the same day.
research_questions: Which notices are still waiting because the shipment id was missing?

already_counted.description: The checking time is already in the broker's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: payment the broker arranged for that shipment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The saving is the re-keying of a notice that already names the shipment. Finding the right account and releasing the money stay with the broker.

tasks.short: Classify goods in the tariff coding system

steps.what: Open the goods description on the invoice
Match goods to a stored tariff decision

loop.purpose: Copy a tariff code only when a stored binding decision matches the goods id.
loop.input: Goods id and the stored decision register.
loop.output: The stored code, or a stop.
loop.check: The code equals the stored decision for that goods id.
loop.stop: Stop when no stored decision matches the goods id.
loop.why_not_simpler: A code with no stored decision cannot be checked against a source.

steps.what: Classify goods in the tariff coding system
File the tariff code the broker signed

tasks.design: Each goods id is looked up in {GOV_PORTAL} for a stored binding decision. A match can be copied. If none matches, the broker classifies in the coding system and signs before {GOV_PORTAL} receives the code.
tasks.previous_blocker: The code was chosen from memory and a paper tariff, with nothing tying it to a decision id.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored decisions can be searched by goods id, so a match is a copy and a miss is visible.
tasks.still_hard: A new product with no decision still needs the broker's classification.
tasks.human_edge: The broker signs the code that will be filed.

ambition.what: A known goods id gets its stored code the day the invoice arrives, and a new goods id still waits for the broker.

tasks.altitude: The broker sees which lines copied a decision and which ones they classified.

reach.learn: Which code was filed for the line.

evidence.claim: Classification is a lookup of a stored decision, and the broker signs every code that is filed. The source pack says duty and tax figures are configured from a public tariff and contracted rates, and that a classification is taken from a stored binding decision only when one matches, with the broker signing the code.

The source pack says a solely automated decision with a significant effect on a person needs a human review. A duty figure here is a stored rate times a stored value, and the broker signs before a filing, a payment, or a quote leaves. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when an invoice line has a goods id and ends when the signed code is filed.
A goods line has goods id, description, and invoice id, produced by the client. A line with no goods id is classified by the broker.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the broker's effort.
A missing rate, code, or document is not invented. The broker does that part.
The incremental hour updates the record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often a goods id already has a binding decision.
research_questions: Which lines stopped because no decision matched?

already_counted.description: The checking time is already in the broker's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: tariff code the broker signed for those goods

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The saving counts only lines whose goods id matches a stored decision. A new description is classified by the broker, and the signature stays.

tasks.short: Clear goods through customs for clients

steps.what: Open the customs entry for the clients
Clear goods through customs for the clients
Note destinations the clearance did not reach
Send the clearance the broker accepted

tasks.design: The entry status is opened in {GOV_PORTAL} from the shipment in {ERP}. The broker clears the goods with the authority. Only a clearance the broker has accepted is sent on, and destinations still open stay on the entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status sat in calls and a mailbox, so nobody could see which destination was still held.
tasks.enabler_now: The entry id carries the latest status, so the broker starts from the hold rather than a retold story.
tasks.still_hard: An official can still hold the goods, and the broker has to answer that hold in person.
tasks.human_edge: The broker accepts the clearance before it is sent.

ambition.what: A held entry is visible the morning it is held, and the broker still clears it.

tasks.altitude: The broker sees which destinations are still short of a clearance.

evidence.claim: Clearance is a status plus a person who deals with the hold. The source pack says duty and tax figures are configured from a public tariff and contracted rates, and that a classification is taken from a stored binding decision only when one matches, with the broker signing the code.

The source pack says a solely automated decision with a significant effect on a person needs a human review. A duty figure here is a stored rate times a stored value, and the broker signs before a filing, a payment, or a quote leaves. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when an entry is waiting for clearance and ends when the broker has accepted that clearance.
The entry has entry id, client id, and destination ids, produced by the shipment file. A destination with no id is handled by the broker.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the broker's effort.
A missing rate, code, or document is not invented. The broker does that part.
The incremental hour updates the record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often an official hold needs a visit rather than a status reply.
research_questions: Which entries are still held after the broker's note?

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: clearance the broker accepted for that entry

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The saving is looking up a status that is already on the entry. The conversation with the authority, and the acceptance, stay with the broker.

tasks.short: Prepare import and export customs documentation

steps.what: Open the import file and the regulations
Prepare import documentation from stored fields

loop.purpose: Fill an import or export paper only from stored document fields.
loop.input: Shipment id and the stored document fields.
loop.output: A draft paper, or a stop.
loop.check: Every filled line equals a stored field for that shipment.
loop.stop: Stop when a required field is missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A paper that invents a missing field cannot be filed.

steps.what: Process export documentation still missing fields
Release the customs papers the broker checked

tasks.design: Required papers are listed from the shipment in {DOCS}. A draft is filled only from stored fields. The broker processes anything still missing and checks the papers before they go to {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Papers were assembled by hand from mail attachments, and a missing certificate showed up late.
tasks.enabler_now: The required-paper list and the stored fields sit on the shipment, so a gap is visible before drafting.
tasks.still_hard: A certificate that has not arrived cannot be invented, and the broker still checks the set.
tasks.human_edge: The broker checks the papers against the regulations before release.

ambition.what: A complete shipment gets its draft the day the fields are stored, and a gap still waits.

tasks.altitude: The broker sees which papers were copied and which fields were missing.

reach.learn: Which paper is still short a field.

evidence.claim: Documentation is a form filled from stored fields, and the broker checks it before it leaves. The source pack says duty and tax figures are configured from a public tariff and contracted rates, and that a classification is taken from a stored binding decision only when one matches, with the broker signing the code.

The source pack says a solely automated decision with a significant effect on a person needs a human review. A duty figure here is a stored rate times a stored value, and the broker signs before a filing, a payment, or a quote leaves. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a shipment needs import or export papers and ends when the broker has checked those papers.
A paper field has shipment id, document type, and value, produced by the client or the carrier. A missing value stops the draft.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the broker's effort.
A missing rate, code, or document is not invented. The broker does that part.

approvals.approved_version: papers the broker checked for that shipment

role.altitude: Duty is a stored rate. The broker signs the tariff code and the papers, and arranges the payment. Clearance of a hold stays with the broker.
reach: A client sees the code that was filed.
A finance manager sees which shipment was paid.
skills_to_grow: Do not invent a tariff code.
Do not file papers that were not checked.
role.ambitious_version: A known goods id is coded the day the invoice arrives, and the broker still signs it.
